status: six completed 39+32-token W8A8 loopback responses with fresh client bundle caches, cached source checkpoints and per-process cold CPU samples; two samples per model/topology

method.bench: ordinary build_roles and run_loopback_benchmark, zero warmups, one response per model/topology, request-sized inventory for prepared placements
method.client_bundle_cache: fresh disposable per run; source safetensors already cached in shared Hugging Face snapshot
method.privacy_audit: zero plaintext prompt and token-ID bytes sent in all three responses
method.compute_scope: sum of authenticated process CPU from child-role birth and benchmark/client startup through the first response; source resolution beforehand excluded

repeat_identity_and_body_check: all three repeated runs preserved their corresponding model fingerprint, token counts, covered online and cold bundle body counts, zero plaintext prompt/token-ID bytes, and prepared stage reconciliation
limitations: Two co-located samples do not establish a representative aggregate-CPU cap; Qwen prepared CPU was higher than the matched offset comparator in both samples. HTTP/TLS/control wire bytes and complete two-worker cold all-link bodies remain unmeasured.
Qwen prepared and offset share a model, W8A8 body fingerprint and token cohort, but remain co-located and cannot establish independent-provider privacy.
SmolLM is a different checkpoint and a different prompt with the same input/output token counts; its byte/CPU differences are not a quality-qualified cross-model ranking.
Source checkpoint downloads, both-worker source distribution, complete disk/cache activity, memory, energy and GPU costs are not included.
